To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mortality impact of persistent extreme heat exposure is additive to the effects based on the ambient temperature–mortality association and the impact of persistent extreme temperatures increases with the length of the extreme heat episode.
persistent extreme high temperatures are associated with additional deaths and that the risk of death increases significantly per day of prolonged heat exposure.
1. The impact of persistent extremely hot weather is associated with an increase of mortality, which is independent of the effect of temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of persistent heatwaves on the mortality of Stockholm County (Sweden) and their implications on models of ambient temperature and mortality.
the impact of extreme heat and cold on mortality and its impact on cause-specific and age-related mortality.
the effects of extreme temperature episodes on mortality and the impact of temperature in general.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
persistent heat exposure increases the risk of cardiovascular mortality and that the effects of non-extreme temperatures are likely to decline over time.
the effect of extreme heat episodes is more harmful than the effect of temperature in general, and the impact of the latter decreases with time.
the effect of temperature and the impact of persistent extreme heat should be considered separately in models of mortality and temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of heatwaves are more severe than the effect of temperature alone.
the effects of temperature on mortality are not only related to the temperature level but also to the duration of the heat exposure.
the effects of temperature on health should be considered in relation to persistence, season and age.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects associated with persistent heat exposure are not only important for cardiovascular deaths, but also for natural deaths.
the effects of extreme heat episodes are important to incorporate in models of mortality related ambient temperatures to avoid underestimating the risk associated with heat waves.
the effect of heatwaves on health and mortality may be underestimated if not properly accounted for in the statistical modelling.
